messages:
Elena (product): Quick sync: several compliance customers asked for a deterministic "handle" from an error card to a reconstructable trace. They want this for audits and to tie to billing disputes. Need scope + launch asks.
Marcus (eng): Two technical options: (A) write a tiny deterministic handle for every request (fixed cost, easy to index), or (B) keep current sampling and write a pointer only on errors (lower steady-state cost but harder to guarantee availability).
Rae (sre): Operational concerns: always-writing handles increases ingest QPS and index size. Pointer-on-error reduces steady IO but creates potential unavailability windows for older data. We can set a hybrid: write handles for paged error-level traffic; sample for bulk.
Priya (acct): From billing side customers need an exportable CSV that ties invoice lines to sample IDs/handles. If we require a paid tier to guarantee full trace exports that's fine, but contract language must be explicit.
Dylan (design): UX thought: show "trace handle" as a compact badge on the error tile. If handle exists, make it clickable and show preview. If not, show "Request reconstruct" CTA and explain expected latency + cost. Keep it minimal.
Elena (product): Proposed prioritization: 1) MVP handle write for errors only (indexable) + simple export mapping invoice_id->handle. 2) Optional always-on handle for enterprise customers as paid add-on. 3) Reconstruction pipeline as an opt-in job queue with audit trail.
Marcus (eng): Rough estimates: (1) error-handle index + API ~1 sprint. (2) always-on handle across ingestion ~2 sprints infra cost. (3) reconstruct queue + export service ~2 sprints + spike to validate cold-read perf. Need spike for retention/backfill impact.
Rae (sre): Ops requirements: per-customer export quotas, background job throttling, a billing-meter for reconstruct CPU/IO, and an alert if reconstruct queue depth grows > threshold. Also require immutable audit entries for each reconstruct/export action.
Priya (acct): Launch gating from finance/legal: exportable CSV mapping handles -> billed lines, clear pricing for reconstruct, and a revocation mechanism. We need legal sign-off for shipping any raw trace export.
Marcus (eng): Implementation notes: handle should be short, deterministic (sha1 of request-id + tenant) and stored in tiny index. Reconstruction will try to rehydrate spans from segmented ingest blobs; if blobs aged out, return failure with audit event. We'll add a cache for recent reconstructions.
Dylan (design): On failure UX: show clear messaging "Full trace unavailable; contact support" + option to queue export if customer has entitlement. Avoid confusing users with partial traces.
Elena (product): Launch criteria draft: - Error handle visible on 95% of error cards for customers with opt-in flag. - Reconstruction attempt success rate >= 90% within 60s for canary tenant. - Export CSV maps invoice lines to handles for pilot customers. - Audit log entry for every reconstruct/export.
Rae (sre): SLOs and throttles: default export SLO 60s for 90% in canary. Global rate limit per-org 5 concurrent reconstruct jobs; burst allowed with backoff. Ops runbook to include cost spike telemetry.
Priya (acct): Business model: free handle+CSV mapping; paid addon for guaranteed always-on handle + priority reconstructs. Will propose pricing tiers and contract language.
Marcus (eng): Action items: I'll open RFC with data model (handle schema), ingestion changes, backfill plan, and reconstruct job design. Need to spike reconstruct with sample dataset.
Dylan (design): I'll put together two small mocks: error-card badge & reconstruct modal, plus a micro-copy doc for failure states.
Elena (product): I'll coordinate pilot customers and legal. Marking this as candidate for Q3 planning.
